title: Yuval Ne'eman, an IDF officer who became a physicist, arranged the elementary particles in a table that predicted a new particle

trailer.text: Yuval Ne'eman, a native of Tel Aviv and a colonel in the Israeli army, was a theoretical physicist, soldier, politician, university president and Israel's minister of science.

Moshe Dayan, then chief of staff, suggested that he pursue his scientific goal through the post of military attaché in London. There Ne'eman had the opportunity to study symmetries in particle physics at Imperial College.
In the early sixties new particles were discovered, and the number of different elementary particles was nearing 100.
Ne'eman's SU(3) classification brought order to them, and was compared to Mendeleyev's periodic table.
Murray Gell-Mann independently published the same discovery shortly after him. In 1964 the omega-minus particle was discovered with the predicted properties, and the discovery confirmed the scheme.

stations.title: A boy from Tel Aviv, an officer on the battlefield

paragraphs.text: Yuval Ne'eman was born on 14 May 1925 in Tel Aviv, to a family that had lived in the country since 1803.
His true intellectual passion was physics.
He studied engineering primarily to satisfy the wish of his family, which wanted him to continue producing water pumps.
At age 15 he enlisted in the Haganah, the Jewish underground organization that later became the Israeli army.
Israel declared its independence on his 23rd birthday, and at that time he was an infantry officer fighting the invading Egyptian army.
After the war he advanced in the army to the rank of colonel.
He headed military planning, and was later promoted to deputy head of military intelligence.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he is credited with formulating the strategic and organizational doctrine of the IDF.

stations.title: One book and a post in London

paragraphs.text: A Hebrew translation of a book by Arthur Eddington rekindled Ne'eman's love of theoretical physics.
Moshe Dayan, then chief of staff, suggested that he pursue his scientific goal through the post of military attaché in London.
In London the busy diplomat had the opportunity to study symmetries in particle physics at Imperial College, where Abdus Salam was the leading figure.
According to Gell-Mann, Ne'eman studied at Imperial College because the embassy in Kensington was close to it.
According to Gell-Mann, this is why he worked in particle physics and not in general relativity.
According to CERN Courier, in May 1960, at the age of 35, Ne'eman left the army to become a full-time graduate student.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in 1958 Ne'eman was appointed defense attaché to Britain and the Scandinavian countries.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Ne'eman continued to serve in the IDF until 1960.
In the early sixties new particles were discovered, and the number of different elementary particles was nearing 100.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, these particles created confusion.
According to CERN Courier, Ne'eman's first major achievement was the use of the SU(3) group as a classifying symmetry for hadrons.
According to an obituary at the Tel Aviv University School of Physics, his contribution was arranging the particles in a kind of periodic array.
According to the same obituary, this array brought order and made it possible to predict additional particles.
Ne'eman's classification was compared to Mendeleyev's periodic table.
Ne'eman completed his doctoral thesis in 1961, at age 36.
Shortly after Ne'eman's publication, Murray Gell-Mann independently published the same discovery.
According to HaYadan, the two arrived at the SU(3) model in parallel and independently.
In 1964 the omega-minus particle was discovered with the predicted properties, and the discovery confirmed the SU(3) scheme.
According to HaYadan, the particle was discovered in February 1964 in the Brookhaven bubble chamber.

According to the Israel Science and Technology website, cited on a University of Texas page, Ne'eman was the first to suggest that particles such as protons and neutrons are made of three fundamental "bricks".
According to Nussinov, Ne'eman and Goldberg introduced entities with baryon number 1/3 in the triplet representation of SU(3).
According to CERN Courier, Ne'eman's paper with Goldberg-Ophir was the first to suggest that an operator with baryon number 1/3 is essential for constructing hadron representations.
The paper by Gell-Mann and Zweig is generally considered the introduction of the idea of quarks.
The Technion credited Ne'eman with discovering the principles of quarks.

stations.title: Building a department, raising a generation

paragraphs.text: According to Physics Today, Ne'eman returned to Israel to create the physics department at the new Tel Aviv University.
After returning to Israel in 1962, Ne'eman began a series of lectures that attracted senior physicists and young students to particle physics.
The lectures attracted senior physicists and young students to particle physics.
His students founded particle-physics groups at other Israeli institutions.
In this way a prominent presence of Israeli theorists emerged in the world.
According to Nussinov, his students and their students make up an almost dominant part of Israeli high energy physicists.
Ne'eman founded the first astrophysics research group in Israel.
In 1971 he founded the Wise Observatory in the Negev.
From 1971 he was president of Tel Aviv University.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Ne'eman resigned as president of Tel Aviv University in 1975.

stations.title: A satellite, the Knesset and scientists behind the curtain

paragraphs.text: In 1983 Ne'eman founded the Israel Space Agency.
He served as its chairman almost until his death.
In 1988 Israel launched its first satellite, while Ne'eman was director of the Space Agency.
He served as a member of the Knesset from 1981 to 1990, and for part of that period was minister of science.
He was the first Israeli minister to meet Soviet President Gorbachev.
According to AP, he is thought to have played an important part in Israel's nuclear program.
Ne'eman was deeply involved in the struggle of Jewish scientists in the Soviet Union for the right to emigrate.
According to Nussinov, he granted the refuseniks positions at Tel Aviv University while they were still in Russia.
According to Nussinov, he also held joint seminars with them by telephone.

stations.title: Recognition, and those who remembered him

paragraphs.text: According to Nussinov, in Israel Ne'eman became a national hero, and popular publications explained the importance of the discovery.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he received the Israel Prize and the Einstein Medal in 1969.
According to the same encyclopaedia, he received the EMET Prize in 2003.
He also received the Wigner Medal.
Sources differ on how many papers and books he published.
He was described as a world-acclaimed physicist, as one of Israel's most prominent scientists and as a right-wing ideologue.
According to Harari, Ne'eman was a very gentle and good-hearted person, contrary to the expected image of an officer and politician.
Ne'eman died on 26 April 2006 in Tel Aviv.
He left a wife, Dvora, a son and a daughter, and a sister, Ruth Ben-Yisrael.

stations.title: Credit that went to another, and stormy politics

paragraphs.text: According to Nussinov, Gell-Mann received most of the credit, and in 1969 won the Nobel Prize alone.
According to Harari, the fact that Gell-Mann and Zweig are considered the ones who introduced the idea of quarks greatly bothered Ne'eman.
According to Harari, Ne'eman felt that much of the idea had already been included in his work with Goldberg.
Ne'eman said he felt great frustration that Gell-Mann had an entire establishment standing behind him, while he had only himself.
According to Nussinov, the Nobel Committee's decision was influenced by the fact that Gell-Mann and Okubo found a mass relation within SU(3) multiplets.
Ne'eman founded Tehiya, a party that broke away from Likud.
In 1992 he returned the Israel Prize in protest at its award to Emile Habibi.
He resigned as senior advisor at the Ministry of Defense in protest over the surrender of the Sinai oilfields in the Interim Agreement with Egypt.

claims.text: לפי ניסינוב, גל-מן קיבל את מרב הקרדיט וב-1969 זכה לבדו בפרס נובל.
claims.quote: However Gell-Mann got most of the credit and in 1969 a Nobel Prize all by himself.

claims.text: לפי הררי, העובדה שגל-מן וצווייג נחשבים למציגי רעיון הקווארקים הטרידה מאוד את נאמן, שחש שחלק גדול מהרעיון כבר נכלל בעבודתו עם גולדברג.
claims.quote: a fact that always bothered Yuval, who felt that much of the idea had already been included in his work with Goldberg.

claims.text: נאמן סיפר שחש תסכול רב מכך שלגל-מן עמד מאחוריו ממסד שלם ולו היה רק עצמו.
claims.quote: I felt great frustration that Gal-Mann had an entire establishment standing behind him and I only had myself.

claims.text: לפי ניסינוב, החלטת ועדת נובל הושפעה מכך שגל-מן ואוקובו מצאו יחס מסות בתוך מולטיפלטים של SU(3).
claims.quote: that Gell-Mann (and also Sossumo Okubo from Rochester) found a relation between masses in SU(3) multiplets embodying a simple pattern of symmetry breaking

claims.text: נאמן התפטר מתפקיד היועץ הבכיר במשרד הביטחון במחאה על ויתור על שדות הנפט בסיני בהסכם הביניים עם מצרים.
claims.quote: he resigned as senior advisor in protest over the surrender of the Sinai (Abu Rudeis) oilfields in the Interim Agreement with Egypt

claims.text: לפי CERN Courier, נאמן ייסד את המחלקה לפיזיקה באוניברסיטת תל אביב ב-1963.
claims.quote: Yuval set up theoretical high energy physics in Israel, founded the physics department at Tel Aviv University in 1963, started the first astrophysics research group in Israel and created the Wise Observatory in the Negev in 1971.

claims.text: לפי הידען, נאמן נפטר בגיל 81.
claims.quote: Prof. Yuval Naman, 81 years old, passed away

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, נאמן נפטר בגיל 80.
claims.quote: Yuval Ne'eman, dean of Israeli scientists, dies at 80

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, ב-1958 מונה נאמן לנספח הביטחון בבריטניה ובמדינות סקנדינביה.
claims.quote: In 1958 he was appointed defense attaché to the uk and the Scandinavian countries.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, נאמן המשיך לשרת בצה"ל עד 1960.
claims.quote: staying on in the idf until 1960.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, נאמן התפטר מנשיאות אוניברסיטת תל אביב ב-1975.
claims.quote: resigned in 1975

claims.text: מ-1971 הוא היה נשיא אוניברסיטת תל אביב.
claims.quote: He served as president of Tel Aviv University (1971-75)

claims.text: נאמן ייסד את התחייה, מפלגה שפרשה מהליכוד.
claims.quote: established in 1979 by Knesset members who had broken away from the Likud

claims.text: נאמן ייסד את התחייה, מפלגה שפרשה מהליכוד.
claims.quote: ב-1979 הקים יחד עם גאולה כהן את תנועת "התחייה" ונבחר לעמוד בראשה.

claims.text: ב-1992 החזיר את פרס ישראל במחאה על הענקתו לאמיל חביבי.
claims.quote: rose from the audience, announced he was returning the Israel Prize for physics

claims.text: ב-1992 החזיר את פרס ישראל במחאה על הענקתו לאמיל חביבי.
claims.quote: the 1992 Israel Prize for Arabic literature
